answer: Account-bound work puzzles. For voyage planning, copper cargo checks, and haven logistics, grant each reward only after a hash of the account, epoch seed, and nonce meets a fixed target. The verifier consumes each proof once and pays per proof, with no account bonus. An attacker pays computing and electricity costs; dividing a fixed hash budget among N identities leaves the expected total reward unchanged. This assumes an unpredictable seed and no reusable shortcuts; specialized hardware can still reduce the cost of work.
